findings.issue: Wrote routes/layout.tsx from memory using <RouterOutlet /> instead of <Slot/>, causing infinite SSR recursion on every route; ~10 turns spent bisecting a self-inflicted bug.
findings.suggestion: When deviating from a scaffolded template pattern, check the framework docs/starter for the layout convention first; the create-qwik template it copied had no layout.tsx to learn from.

findings.issue: `pkill -f 'vite preview'` matched its own bash command line and killed the shell (exit 143).
findings.suggestion: Kill by recorded PID or use a pattern that can't match the current shell (e.g. pkill -f 'node_modules/.bin/vite').

findings.issue: Two file writes fail with 'No such file or directory' because target directories weren't created first.
findings.suggestion: mkdir -p before writing, or write via a file-creation tool rather than bash heredocs.

findings.issue: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS from agent-browser after setting trailingSlash:false; never diagnosed, just retried until it worked.
findings.suggestion: Reproduce with curl and inspect response headers/redirect chain before retrying; likely a stale browser tab hitting a mid-restart server.

findings.issue: Researched setting HTTP 404 status (spec encourages it), then declined and instead made an unrelated sprite change in the same edit pass.
findings.suggestion: Either implement status(404) in the loaders/catchall or leave a note; the ambiguity is resolved without a decision being recorded.

findings.issue: Heredoc/python quoting messes (broken here-document delimiter; SyntaxError on embedded CSS) cost three turns.
findings.suggestion: Use single-purpose, quoted edits per command; avoid interleaving multiple heredocs in one bash call.

summary: A strong, well-sequenced session: the agent read the spec, every test file, the data shapes and all reference screenshots before writing code, then produced ~1500 lines that passed 51/54 on the first run and 54/54 after one targeted fix, finishing with a full-suite pass after its last edit. Its verification was exceptional — full test runs, curl probes of every route, both-width screenshots, pixel-run measurements against references, and manual checks of URL-state behavior the tests don't cover. The main blemishes are self-inflicted: the RouterOutlet-instead-of-Slot recursion that cost ~10 turns to bisect, and a handful of careless shell mistakes (self-killing pkill, two mkdir misses, heredoc breakage) rather than bad direction.
